rights_holder.current_claimed: The 2026 karenware.com footer reads 'Copyright ©1997-2026 Karen Kenworthy, Joe Winett - All Rights Reserved'. The site's contact page says Karen bequeathed the site and her intellectual properties to family member Terry Starr, and that Joe Winett operates the site.

period_notice: The 2003 page embedding the image carries 'Copyright © 1997-2003 Karen Kenworthy All Rights Reserved'; the 2001 page carries 'Copyright © 2001 Karen Kenworthy All Rights Reserved'.
license_terms: No license, public-domain dedication, or media/press permission for website images or screenshots was found. The karenware.com licensing page covers use of the programs (free for personal and educational use; a paid license for work use). That is a software-use license and does not grant reuse of the screenshot in a published video. The site's 'Open Source Licenses' page lists only third-party web components (Bootstrap, PHPMailer, Timeago, html2text).
archive_terms_note: Internet Archive availability is not a license. The archive holds a copy; the copyright stays with the original rights holder.
rights_status: blocked — all rights reserved; no permission on record
fair_use_assessment: Not made. Whether a short, credited use of this screenshot in a commentary video is acceptable is a legal-risk question for Devin, not an agent decision.

handoff.type: permission request (human boundary: sending a message on Devin's behalf)
handoff.note: None of H01–H07 covers archival image permission, so this is a specific new human handoff.
handoff.who: Joe Winett, karenware.com site operator, who says he acts for Karen Kenworthy's heir Terry Starr. The site's contact page (evidence/captures/karenware-20260915-contact.html) lists his contact address.
handoff.ask: Written permission to show the karenware.com Window Watcher screenshot (ptwinwatch.gif, 489x448) unaltered in a YouTube video about Visual Basic history, with the credit line in evidence/source.json, or the credit they prefer.
handoff.alternative: Devin makes a recorded fair-use decision, or drops this image from the collage.
